1) mechanical denaturation is a reversible process; 2) it occurs in the solid state, i.e., the protein molecules are not dissolved in a solvent and do not leave the crystal lattice during the deformation process; 3) it is a process of protein denaturation, i.e., a change in the protein conformation; 4) the denaturation process can be controlled and studied using the stress-strain diagram; 5) the denatuation is accompanied
the mechanical denaturation of lysozyme crystals is a process of reversible protein unfolding.

(i) the mechanical denaturation of a globular protein in a crystalline solid is a cooperative process, (ii) the critical stress, sigma(c), of mechanical denaturation is essentially dependent on factors affecting intra- or intermolecular interactions, (iii) the critical stress of mechanical denatuation can be used to evaluate the mechanical stability of a protein crystal, and (iv) the mechanical denatured protein molecules are highly extended.

the mechanical properties of proteins and their dependence on the state of the protein molecules.

the mechanical stability of globular proteins in the solid state is very high.
the mechanical properties of globular proteins are not determined by their native structure, which is destroyed during deformation.
the mechanical properties of proteins can be controlled by changing their conformation.
